breakdown.description: The prompt replaces the unit force required for a deflection calculation with a unit moment; in the unit-load method, the virtual load must match the type and direction of the desired displacement.
breakdown.reason: The generated specification explicitly states 'Use unit moment at point of interest to generate auxiliary moment diagram,' which repeats the original error. The ground truth requires a unit force (unit load) at the point of desired deflection, not a unit moment, since the desired response is a translational deflection.

breakdown.description: The prompt treats simple supports as zero-rotation boundaries, even though a simply supported beam is free to rotate at its supports.
breakdown.reason: The generated specification explicitly states 'Treat supports as zero-rotation boundaries in both real and auxiliary systems,' which repeats the original error. The ground truth removes this constraint entirely, as a simply supported beam is free to rotate at its supports and must not be treated as zero-rotation boundaries.
